items.excerpt: Three Epic Games veterans — including former Unreal lead evangelist Sjoerd De Jong and ex-Unreal product director Arjan Brussee — detail Immens, a European game engine whose architecture, tooling and asset pipelines are built from scratch around AI agents rather than bolting AI on. They pitch it as a way for small teams to cut cost and dev time amid mounting discontent with Unity and Unreal.

Wolf Haus's co-founders explain how a 12-person team is shipping the large-scale cult simulator Join Us using in-house tech and explicitly no generative AI — a counter-case to the 'AI lets small teams do AAA' pitch, arguing custom tooling and Hollywood-style production discipline do the same job.

Game Developer's read on the same 100-speaker Gamescom Dev survey: developers expect generative AI to reshape which roles exist and how big teams get, with the sharpest effects landing on art, QA and production support rather than on core design.

Players in China spotted a free-trial watermark for ByteDance's Doubao AI image tool left on in-game seahorse artwork in Neverness To Everness' 1.3 update — an accidental disclosure of generative AI in a shipped live-service art pipeline.

A long feature on generative AI inside the Skyrim modding scene, reported from the perspective of players, modders and the mod-hosting sites themselves — including why disclosure tagging keeps failing and how UGC platforms are struggling to build workable AI policy.

A Witcher 3 lead on the craft of NPC reaction systems: an ambitious fear-response behaviour had to be cut after weeks of grotesque emergent failures, a cautionary tale for anyone now wiring LLM-driven NPC autonomy into open worlds.

CD Projekt Red couldn't ship the NPC fear-reaction system it prototyped for The Witcher 3 because emergent crowd behaviour broke in horrifying ways — a concrete case study in how hard believable autonomous NPC behaviour actually is to tune.

Rideshare Stimulator's Steam genAI disclosure finally lands and reveals a wider footprint than admitted — generative tech is used for in-game music as well as writing — while Saber's CEO frames genAI adoption as 'swim or die' for studios.

Saber Interactive publishes a breakdown of exactly where AI was used on Rideshare Stimulator after former lead writer Stella Sacco said she had been replaced by ChatGPT — a rare, itemised studio disclosure of genAI in a shipping production.

Saber CEO Matthew Karch privately apologises to writer Stella Sacco after publicly saying he would have been happy to replace her with AI — the closing beat of the industry's loudest current fight over genAI in narrative roles.

After apologising for gen-AI art assets spotted in 1666: Amsterdam, the studio confirms it is still using AI tools in production — 'we live in a world full of AI, let's be honest with ourselves' — and explains where in the art pipeline they sit.

Aftermath's reported follow-up on 1666: Amsterdam quotes the developer's economic argument for AI in concept work — 'I can ask the AI to give me 75 different variations of one thing, but I cannot have 75 different illustrators come up with a variation in three seconds' — and weighs it against what the game actually shipped.

With Twitch declining to label which streams use AI or were opted into AI training, streamers are building their own disclosure vocabulary — tags like AIOptedOut, NoGenAI and NoAI — creating a bottom-up provenance standard on a games platform.

Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki argues that as AI-generated content floods creative fields, players will increasingly seek out demonstrably human-made work — a platform-holder signal on how PlayStation may position craft and authorship as product value.
